title: Symmetrical Designs: Reflection, Rotation and Symmetry
seo_title: Reflection, Rotation and Symmetry Class 5 Worksheet with Answers (Maths Mela Chapter 10)
standard_code: Class 5, Maths Mela Chapter 10: Symmetrical Designs
standard_text: Symmetry: reflection (line) symmetry and rotational symmetry in designs, and making symmetric patterns by flipping and turning (summary of NCERT Maths Mela Class 5)
meta_desc: Class 5 Symmetrical Designs worksheet (Maths Mela Chapter 10): reflections, rotations, flips and turns and symmetric designs. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A reflection flips a shape over a mirror line.
key_sub: A rotation turns it about a point.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A reflection (flip) makes a mirror image across a line.
  • A rotation (turn) turns a shape about a point: quarter, half or full turn.
  • Many rangoli designs have both kinds of symmetry.

Examples

Example

A shape looks the same after a half turn.

It fits twice in a full turn

Answer: It has rotational symmetry of order 2

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Shifting instead of flippingEach point moves to the same distance on the other side of the mirror.
Turning the wrong wayClockwise is the way clock hands move.

faq.a: A shape has it if it looks the same after a turn of less than a full turn.
A flip over a mirror line.

items.q: Reflect the point (3, 4) in the vertical line x = 5. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (3, 4) is 2 units to the left of the line x = 5. The image is 2 units to the right of it: 5 + 2 = 7. y stays 4. The image is (7, 4).

items.q: Reflect the point (8, 2) in the vertical line x = 6. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (8, 2) is 2 units to the right of the line x = 6. The image is 2 units to the left of it: 6 − 2 = 4. y stays 2. The image is (4, 2).

items.q: Reflect the point (2, 1) in the horizontal line y = 3. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (2, 1) is 2 units below the line y = 3. The image is 2 units above it: 3 + 2 = 5. x stays 2. The image is (2, 5).

items.q: Reflect the point (6, 9) in the horizontal line y = 6. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (6, 9) is 3 units above the line y = 6. The image is 3 units below it: 6 − 3 = 3. x stays 6. The image is (6, 3).

items.q: Reflect the point (1, 7) in the vertical line x = 4. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (1, 7) is 3 units to the left of the line x = 4. The image is 3 units to the right of it: 4 + 3 = 7. y stays 7. The image is (7, 7).

items.q: Reflect the point (5, 3) in the horizontal line y = 5. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (5, 3) is 2 units below the line y = 5. The image is 2 units above it: 5 + 2 = 7. x stays 5. The image is (5, 7).

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the line x = 4?
items.e: P (2, 3) is 2 units to the left of the line x = 4. The image is 2 units to the right of it: 4 + 2 = 6. y stays 3. The image is (6, 3). That is point B. Point A: it is 1 unit too far (the grid lines were counted, starting with 1 on P’s line). Point C: it stops on the line of reflection. Point D: it was flipped up or down, not across the line.

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the line x = 5?
items.e: P (7, 5) is 2 units to the right of the line x = 5. The image is 2 units to the left of it: 5 − 2 = 3. y stays 5. The image is (3, 5). That is point A. Point B: it is 1 unit too far (the grid lines were counted, starting with 1 on P’s line). Point C: it stops on the line of reflection. Point D: x and y are swapped.

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the line y = 3?
items.e: P (3, 1) is 2 units below the line y = 3. The image is 2 units above it: 3 + 2 = 5. x stays 3. The image is (3, 5). That is point D. Point A: it is 1 unit too far (the grid lines were counted, starting with 1 on P’s line). Point B: it stops on the line of reflection. Point C: x and y are swapped.

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the line y = 4?
items.e: P (5, 6) is 2 units above the line y = 4. The image is 2 units below it: 4 − 2 = 2. x stays 5. The image is (5, 2). That is point C. Point A: it is 1 unit too far (the grid lines were counted, starting with 1 on P’s line). Point B: it stops on the line of reflection. Point D: it was flipped across, not up or down over the line.

items.q: Reflect the point (3, 4) in the vertical mirror line x = 5. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (3, 4) is 2 squares to the left of the line x = 5. The image is 2 squares to the right of it: 5 + 2 = 7. y stays 4. The image is (7, 4).

items.q: Reflect the point (8, 2) in the vertical mirror line x = 6. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (8, 2) is 2 squares to the right of the line x = 6. The image is 2 squares to the left of it: 6 − 2 = 4. y stays 2. The image is (4, 2).

items.q: Reflect the point (2, 1) in the horizontal mirror line y = 3. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (2, 1) is 2 squares below the line y = 3. The image is 2 squares above it: 3 + 2 = 5. x stays 2. The image is (2, 5).

items.q: Reflect the point (6, 9) in the horizontal mirror line y = 6. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (6, 9) is 3 squares above the line y = 6. The image is 3 squares below it: 6 − 3 = 3. x stays 6. The image is (6, 3).

items.q: Reflect the point (1, 7) in the vertical mirror line x = 4. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (1, 7) is 3 squares to the left of the line x = 4. The image is 3 squares to the right of it: 4 + 3 = 7. y stays 7. The image is (7, 7).

items.q: Reflect the point (5, 3) in the horizontal mirror line y = 5. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (5, 3) is 2 squares below the line y = 5. The image is 2 squares above it: 5 + 2 = 7. x stays 5. The image is (5, 7).

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the mirror line x = 4?
items.e: P (2, 3) is 2 squares to the left of the line x = 4. The image is 2 squares to the right of it: 4 + 2 = 6. y stays 3. The image is (6, 3). That is point A. Point B: it is 1 square too far (the lines were counted, starting with 1 on the line P is on). Point C: it stops on the mirror line. Point D: it was flipped up or down, not across the line.

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the mirror line x = 5?
items.e: P (7, 5) is 2 squares to the right of the line x = 5. The image is 2 squares to the left of it: 5 − 2 = 3. y stays 5. The image is (3, 5). That is point D. Point A: it is 1 square too far (the lines were counted, starting with 1 on the line P is on). Point B: it stops on the mirror line. Point C: x and y are swapped.

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the mirror line y = 3?
items.e: P (3, 1) is 2 squares below the line y = 3. The image is 2 squares above it: 3 + 2 = 5. x stays 3. The image is (3, 5). That is point C. Point A: it is 1 square too far (the lines were counted, starting with 1 on the line P is on). Point B: it stops on the mirror line. Point D: x and y are swapped.

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the mirror line y = 4?
items.e: P (5, 6) is 2 squares above the line y = 4. The image is 2 squares below it: 4 − 2 = 2. x stays 5. The image is (5, 2). That is point B. Point A: it is 1 square too far (the lines were counted, starting with 1 on the line P is on). Point C: it stops on the mirror line. Point D: it was flipped across, not up or down over the line.

items.q: How many degrees is a quarter turn?
items.e: A full turn is 360°. A quarter turn is one of 4 equal parts: 360° ÷ 4 = 90°. A half turn is 180°.

items.q: Which way do the hands of a clock turn?
items.e: Clock hands go from 12 to 3 to 6 to 9: that is clockwise. The other way is anticlockwise.

items.q: A triangle is rotated about its vertex A. Which point stays in the same place?
items.e: The centre of rotation does not move. Here the centre is vertex A; every other point turns around it.

items.q: A shape is rotated 180° clockwise about a point. A copy of it is rotated 180° anticlockwise about the same point. Where do they land?
c: one lands twice as far away
one is a mirror image of the other
items.e: A half turn is a half turn, whichever way you go. 180° clockwise and 180° anticlockwise end in the same place.

items.q: Rotate the point B (6, 4) 90° clockwise about the point A (3, 4). Where does B land?
items.e: From A (3, 4), B (6, 4) is 3 right. In a 90° clockwise turn, right turns into down, down into left, left into up and up into right. So from (3, 4), the image is 3 down: (3, 1).

items.q: A triangle has vertices A (4, 4), B (4, 7) and C (6, 4). It is rotated 90° clockwise about vertex A. Where does vertex B land?
items.e: From vertex A (4, 4), vertex B (4, 7) is 3 up. In a 90° clockwise turn, right turns into down, down into left, left into up and up into right. So from (4, 4), the image is 3 right: (7, 4).

items.q: Rotate the point Q (8, 5) 90° anticlockwise about the point P (5, 5). Where does Q land?
items.e: From P (5, 5), Q (8, 5) is 3 right. In a 90° anticlockwise turn, right turns into up, up into left, left into down and down into right. So from (5, 5), the image is 3 up: (5, 8).

items.q: A rectangle has vertices K (3, 3), L (5, 3), M (5, 6) and N (3, 6). It is rotated 90° clockwise about vertex K. Where does vertex M land?
items.e: From vertex K (3, 3), vertex M (5, 6) is 2 right and 3 up. In a 90° clockwise turn, right turns into down, down into left, left into up and up into right. So from (3, 3), the image is 3 right and 2 down: (6, 1).

items.q: A triangle has vertices D (5, 3), E (2, 4) and F (5, 6). It is rotated 90° anticlockwise about vertex D. Where does vertex E land?
items.e: From vertex D (5, 3), vertex E (2, 4) is 3 left and 1 up. In a 90° anticlockwise turn, right turns into up, up into left, left into down and down into right. So from (5, 3), the image is 1 left and 3 down: (4, 0).

items.q: Rotate the point S (8, 5) 180° about the point R (6, 4). Where does S land?
items.e: From R (6, 4), S (8, 5) is 2 right and 1 up. In a 180° turn, right turns into left, left into right, up into down and down into up. So from (6, 4), the image is 2 left and 1 down: (4, 3).

items.q: Point P is rotated a quarter turn clockwise about point O. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: From O (4, 5), P (7, 5) is 3 right. In a quarter turn clockwise, right turns into down, down into left, left into up and up into right. So the image is 3 down from O: (4, 2). That is point A. Point B: turned a quarter turn anticlockwise. Point C: turned a half turn. Point D: turned the right way, but 1 square too far from O.

items.q: Point P is rotated a quarter turn clockwise about point O. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: From O (5, 3), P (5, 6) is 3 up. In a quarter turn clockwise, right turns into down, down into left, left into up and up into right. So the image is 3 right from O: (8, 3). That is point C. Point A: turned a quarter turn anticlockwise. Point B: turned a half turn. Point D: turned the right way, but 1 square too far from O.

items.q: Point P is rotated a quarter turn anticlockwise about point O. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: From O (4, 5), P (6, 6) is 2 right, 1 up. In a quarter turn anticlockwise, right turns into up, up into left, left into down and down into right. So the image is 1 left, 2 up from O: (3, 7). That is point B. Point A: turned a quarter turn clockwise. Point C: turned a half turn. Point D: flipped in a mirror line, not turned.

items.q: Point P is rotated a half turn about point O. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: From O (5, 4), P (7, 6) is 2 right, 2 up. In a half turn, right turns into left and up turns into down. So the image is 2 left, 2 down from O: (3, 2). That is point D. Point A: turned a quarter turn clockwise. Point B: turned a quarter turn anticlockwise. Point C: turned the right way, but 1 square too far from O.

items.q: Shape A is moved to shape B. Point O does not move. What happened to shape A?
items.e: Follow the side that starts at O. In A it goes from O to (8, 4) and points right. In B the matching side goes to (5, 1) and points down. Right to down is a quarter turn clockwise.

items.q: Shape A is moved to shape B. Point O does not move. What happened to shape A?
items.e: Follow the side that starts at O. In A it goes from O to (4, 7) and points up. In B the matching side goes to (1, 4) and points left. Up to left is a quarter turn anticlockwise.

items.q: Shape A is moved to shape B. Point O does not move. What happened to shape A?
items.e: Follow the side that starts at O. In A it goes from O to (8, 4) and points right. In B the matching side goes to (2, 4) and points left. Right to left is a half turn.

items.q: Shape A is moved to shape B. Point O does not move. What happened to shape A?
items.e: B is a mirror image of A in the vertical line through O: every corner stays at the same height, for example (7, 6) → (3, 6). A turn about O would keep the shape the same way round; this one is flipped.

items.q: Shape A is moved to shape B. Point O does not move. What happened to shape A?
items.e: Follow the side that starts at O. In A it goes from O to (4, 6) and points up. In B the matching side goes to (7, 3) and points right. Up to right is a quarter turn clockwise.

items.q: Shape A is moved to shape B. Point O does not move. What happened to shape A?
items.e: Follow the side that starts at O. In A it goes from O to (8, 4) and points right. In B the matching side goes to (5, 7) and points up. Right to up is a quarter turn anticlockwise.

items.q: What does a flip (reflection) make?
c: the same shape, facing the same way
a smaller copy of the shape
a bigger copy of the shape
a mirror image of the shape
items.e: A flip turns the shape over a line, like a mirror. The image faces the other way, but its size does not change.

items.q: Point P is 3 units to the left of a vertical line of reflection. Where is its image?
c: 3 units to the left of the line
6 units to the right of the line
3 units to the right of the line
2 units to the right of the line
items.e: In a flip the image is the same distance from the line as the point, on the other side. (2 units comes from counting the line as the first jump.)

items.q: Point P is flipped in the dashed line x = 4. Which point is its image?
items.e: P (2, 3) is 2 units to the left of the line x = 4. The image is 2 units to the right of it: 4 + 2 = 6. y stays 3. The image is (6, 3). That is point C. Point A: it is 1 unit too close to the line (the line was counted as the first jump). Point B: it was flipped up or down, not across the line. Point D: x and y are swapped.

items.q: Point P is flipped in the dashed line x = 5. Which point is its image?
items.e: P (8, 6) is 3 units to the right of the line x = 5. The image is 3 units to the left of it: 5 − 3 = 2. y stays 6. The image is (2, 6). That is point D. Point A: it is 1 unit too close to the line (the line was counted as the first jump). Point B: it stops on the line of reflection. Point C: x and y are swapped.

items.q: Point P is flipped in the dashed line y = 3. Which point is its image?
items.e: P (2, 1) is 2 units below the line y = 3. The image is 2 units above it: 3 + 2 = 5. x stays 2. The image is (2, 5). That is point B. Point A: it is 1 unit too close to the line (the line was counted as the first jump). Point C: x and y are swapped. Point D: it was flipped across, not up or down over the line.

items.q: Point P is flipped in the dashed line y = 4. Which point is its image?
items.e: P (5, 6) is 2 units above the line y = 4. The image is 2 units below it: 4 − 2 = 2. x stays 5. The image is (5, 2). That is point A. Point B: it is 1 unit too close to the line (the line was counted as the first jump). Point C: it was flipped across, not up or down over the line. Point D: x and y are swapped.

items.q: The green shape is flipped (reflected) in the dashed line. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: Each vertex of the image must be the same distance from the line as its partner, on the other side. Only B is a true mirror image. Others: A: the image is 1 unit too close to the line (the line was counted as the first jump); C: the shape was turned (it is upside down and back to front), not flipped; D: the shape was slid across, not flipped (it faces the same way).

items.q: The green shape is flipped (reflected) in the dashed line. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: Each vertex of the image must be the same distance from the line as its partner, on the other side. Only A is a true mirror image. Others: B: the shape was turned (it is upside down and back to front), not flipped; C: the image is 1 unit too close to the line (the line was counted as the first jump); D: the shape was flipped the wrong way (left to right), not over the dashed line.

items.q: The green shape is flipped (reflected) in the dashed line. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: Each vertex of the image must be the same distance from the line as its partner, on the other side. Only D is a true mirror image. Others: A: the image is 1 unit too far from the line; B: the shape was turned (it is upside down and back to front), not flipped; C: the shape was slid across, not flipped (it faces the same way).

items.q: Reflect the point (5, 3) in the vertical line x = 5. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (5, 3) is on the line of reflection x = 5, so it does not move: (5, 3). A point on the line of reflection is its own image.

items.q: The minute hand of a clock moves from 12 to 3. What turn is that?
items.e: From 12 to 3 is one quarter of the way around the clock, and clock hands move clockwise.

items.q: A triangle is turned about its vertex A. Which point stays in the same place?
items.e: The centre of rotation (the turn centre) does not move. Here it is vertex A; every other point turns around it.

items.q: A shape makes two quarter turns clockwise about the same point. What is that the same as?
items.e: Each quarter turn is 90°. 90° + 90° = 180°, which is a half turn.

items.q: A shape is turned 180° clockwise about a point. A copy of it is turned 180° anticlockwise about the same point. Where do they land?
c: one lands twice as far away
one is a mirror image of the other
items.e: A half turn is a half turn, whichever way you go. 180° clockwise and 180° anticlockwise end in the same place.

items.q: Turn the point B (6, 4) 90° clockwise about the point A (3, 4). Where does B land?
items.e: From A (3, 4), B (6, 4) is 3 right. In a 90° clockwise turn, right turns into down, down into left, left into up and up into right. So from (3, 4), the image is 3 down: (3, 1).

items.q: Turn the point Q (8, 5) 90° anticlockwise about the point P (5, 5). Where does Q land?
items.e: From P (5, 5), Q (8, 5) is 3 right. In a 90° anticlockwise turn, right turns into up, up into left, left into down and down into right. So from (5, 5), the image is 3 up: (5, 8).

items.q: A rectangle has vertices K (3, 3), L (5, 3), M (5, 6) and N (3, 6). It is turned 90° clockwise about vertex K. Where does vertex M land?
items.e: From vertex K (3, 3), vertex M (5, 6) is 2 right and 3 up. In a 90° clockwise turn, right turns into down, down into left, left into up and up into right. So from (3, 3), the image is 3 right and 2 down: (6, 1).

items.q: A triangle has vertices A (4, 4), B (1, 5) and C (4, 7). It is turned 180° about vertex A. Where does vertex B land?
items.e: From vertex A (4, 4), vertex B (1, 5) is 3 left and 1 up. In a 180° turn, right turns into left, left into right, up into down and down into up. So from (4, 4), the image is 3 right and 1 down: (7, 3).

items.q: The green shape is turned 90° clockwise about the red dot. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: The red dot does not move. Follow one side: the side from the red dot going right turns to go down in a quarter turn (90°) clockwise. Only A shows that. Others: B: a quarter turn anticlockwise; C: a flip (mirror image), not a turn; D: a half turn (180°).

items.q: The green shape is turned 90° anticlockwise about the red dot. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: The red dot does not move. Follow one side: the side from the red dot going right turns to go up in a quarter turn (90°) anticlockwise. Only B shows that. Others: A: a quarter turn clockwise; C: a flip (mirror image), not a turn; D: a half turn (180°).

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: B faces the same way as A and is the same size. Every vertex moved 5 units right and 3 units up, for example (1, 1) → (6, 4). That is a translation.

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: In A the long arm of the L lies flat along the bottom. In B it stands straight up. A slide or a flip cannot make a flat arm stand up, but a turn can: B is A turned 90° clockwise about the vertex (5, 5).

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: B is A turned upside down and back to front: a half turn (180°) about the vertex (5, 2). A single flip would change only one of these.

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: In A the right angle is at the bottom left; in B it is at the top left. B is A flipped over the line y = 4: each vertex is the same distance from the line on the other side, for example (2, 5) → (2, 3). That is a reflection.

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: A is 4 units by 2 units. B is only 2 units by 1 unit, so B is smaller. A translation, a reflection or a rotation never changes the size.

items.q: In a coding lesson, Ananya’s robot starts at (1, 2). The code says: move 4 right, then move 3 up. Where does the robot stop?
items.e: Right 4 changes x: 1 + 4 = 5. Up 3 changes y: 2 + 3 = 5. The new point is (5, 5).

items.q: Kabir’s robot is at (2, 7). He wants it to stop at (6, 3). Which code works?
items.e: The start is at (2, 7) and the end is at (6, 3). Across: 2 to 6 is 4 units right. Up and down: 7 to 3 is 4 units down. Count the spaces you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: In a board game, each turn moves a counter 2 units right. Riya’s counter starts at (1, 4). Where is it after 3 turns?
items.e: 3 turns is 3 × 2 = 6 units right. x: 1 + 6 = 7. y stays 4. The counter is at (7, 4).

items.q: On a map of a campsite, the fire pit is at (3, 5) and the canoe dock is at (8, 1). Describe the translation from the fire pit to the dock.
items.e: The fire pit is at (3, 5) and the dock is at (8, 1). Across: 3 to 8 is 5 units right. Up and down: 5 to 1 is 4 units down. Count the spaces you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: On a hockey play diagram, Kavya skates from (2, 3), 6 units right and 4 units up. Where does she stop?
items.e: Right 6 changes x: 2 + 6 = 8. Up 4 changes y: 3 + 4 = 7. The new point is (8, 7).

items.q: Which transformation is most like SkyTrain moving along a straight piece of track?
items.e: The train moves in a straight line and does not turn or flip, so it is a slide.

items.q: Which transformation is most like the mountains and their upside-down picture in a calm lake?
items.e: The picture in the water is a mirror image, upside down over the shoreline. That is a flip.

items.q: Which transformation is most like a door swinging open on its hinges?
items.e: The door turns about the hinges. The hinges stay still, like a turn centre. That is a turn.

items.q: Which transformation is most like pushing a box straight across the gym floor?
items.e: The box moves across without turning or flipping, so it is a slide.

items.q: Which transformation is most like the hands of a clock moving from 12 to 6?
items.e: The hands turn about the centre of the clock. That is a half turn.

items.q: Which transformation is most like your hand and its image in a mirror?
items.e: A mirror image faces the other way: a right hand looks like a left hand. That is a flip.

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: In A the long arm of the L lies flat along the bottom. In B it stands straight up. A slide or a flip cannot make a flat arm stand up, but a turn can: B is A turned a quarter turn (90°) clockwise.

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: B looks exactly like A and faces the same way. Every vertex moved 5 units right and 4 units down. That is a slide.

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: Follow the top edge of A, from (1, 5) to (5, 5): it goes across. In B the same edge goes up and down, from (6, 1) to (6, 5). A slide or a flip cannot do that, but a turn can: B is A turned a quarter turn (90°) anticlockwise.

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: In A the long side is at the bottom; in B it is at the top, and the square corners are still on the left. That is a mirror image over the line y = 4: a flip. A half turn would also move the square corners to the right.

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the mirror line x = 4?
items.e: P (2, 3) is 2 squares to the left of the line x = 4. The image is 2 squares to the right of it: 4 + 2 = 6. y stays 3. The image is (6, 3). That is point D. Point A: it is 1 square too far (the lines were counted, starting with 1 on the line P is on). Point B: it stops on the mirror line. Point C: it was flipped up or down, not across the line.

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the mirror line x = 5?
items.e: P (7, 5) is 2 squares to the right of the line x = 5. The image is 2 squares to the left of it: 5 − 2 = 3. y stays 5. The image is (3, 5). That is point A. Point B: it is 1 square too far (the lines were counted, starting with 1 on the line P is on). Point C: it stops on the mirror line. Point D: x and y are swapped.

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the mirror line y = 3?
items.e: P (3, 1) is 2 squares below the line y = 3. The image is 2 squares above it: 3 + 2 = 5. x stays 3. The image is (3, 5). That is point B. Point A: it is 1 square too far (the lines were counted, starting with 1 on the line P is on). Point C: it stops on the mirror line. Point D: x and y are swapped.

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the mirror line y = 4?
